text:
Philadelphia is 9-12-6, last-ten form of 5-3-2, and our numbers give it a 7% chance at the playoffs. The trouble is plain at five on five, where the Flyers get only 43% of expected goals (the quality of chances each side gets), and in net, where Dan Vladar (.850 over his last five) and Joseph Woll (.860) are both struggling. A 7-3 loss in Washington on Wednesday was, in Charlie O'Connor's word, ugly.

The bigger story is who stays. Travis Konecny's name is all over the trade rumor sites, with Montreal and Ottawa floated, and Yahoo Sports ran a piece arguing he shouldn't have to answer questions about his commitment. Matvei Michkov has been asked about too; Markerzone reported Daniel Briere's answer was no. That tells you where the line is: the young core is not for sale.

And the young core is where the good news lives. Noah Cates, Michkov and Porter Martone have been the best line, 62% of the chances, and Cates scored the winner against Montreal with 31 seconds left. Denver Barkey has eight points in ten and keeps getting praise from Rick Tocchet for his work at center. The concern is Trevor Zegras, one point in ten against 6.7 expected. For a rebuilding team, a lost season is fine. A lost season for the players who are supposed to be next is not.
headline: The Flyers are rebuilding in public
